name: CHARS
desc: Covers CHARS: Unicode codepoint sets, inclusive integer/string/null ranges, character lists including empty lists, ordered inclusion/exclusion, initial complement semantics, nested common CHARS expressions, numeric and one-codepoint string targets, regex and array-sequence consumption, lexical scopes, captures, SPLIT/JOIN integration, operand validation, and resource failures. Expected memberships are defined independently of representation. Surrogate-dependent cases carry explicit compatibility flags.

tests.name: Lists and initial state
tests.desc: The default set is empty. Only a false operand in the first position starts from all Unicode; later booleans change the operation without changing existing members. One-codepoint strings and integers are equivalent endpoints, while multi-codepoint strings are unordered character lists.

tests.name: Later true preserves the initial universe
Empty operand before false prevents initial complement
A class consumes one character only
Trailing exclusion does not alter existing members
Trailing exclusion does not create other members
Inclusive ranges and Unicode boundaries
tests.desc: Adjacent singleton operands pair greedily into inclusive ranges. Null denotes U+10FFFF, including as a lower endpoint. Surrogate codepoint values are legal members; string matching depends on the host exposing lone surrogates.

tests.name: Surrogate members do not split valid pairs
BMP noncharacter is a legal member
Ordered inclusion and exclusion
tests.desc: Each range/list/class is applied in order. Exclusion subtracts from the existing set, inclusion can restore removed members, and repeated or adjacent spans remain ordinary sets. Mode changes alone do not invert existing members.

tests.name: Split a range then restore one point
Ordinary targets
tests.desc: Outside regex context CHARS accepts a valid integer codepoint or a string of exactly one codepoint. Other target types, out-of-range numbers, empty strings, and multi-codepoint strings do not match. It performs no coercion and never consumes only a prefix of an ordinary string.

tests.name: Lone surrogate strings are one codepoint
Ordinary strings are not searched for members
Alternate target changes back to ordinary matching
Missing current node does not match
Common CHARS expressions
tests.desc: Only EXPR operands may import another CHARS set. Their sets are unioned/subtracted using the current outer mode, retaining inner complement/exclusion semantics. Names resolve in lexical scope at invocation time, and computed names must not be cached as constants.

tests.name: Child exclusion does not delete parent members
Outer exclusion respects holes in child
Boolean modes stay local to child
Computed names depend on current character
Shadowed definitions do not reuse parent sets
Root EXPR CHARS retains regex semantics
Composition and consumption
tests.desc: CHARS consumes exactly one character/element when it matches and none when it fails. Sequences, repetition, alternatives, assertions, captures, and SPLIT/JOIN use the same membership rules. Empty classes never match the end boundary.

tests.name: Repeated digits span the entire string
Repeated digits reject an interior letter
Zero repetitions allow the empty string
Complete class cannot consume the end
Following term starts at the next character
ANY recovers from a failed class
Array sequence accepts strings and integers
Array class does not consume multi-character strings
CASE can use an ordinary class predicate
SPLIT and JOIN use a class separator
Invalid operands and failures
tests.desc: Only booleans, strings, valid integer codepoints, null, and EXPR resolving to CHARS are operands. Descending ranges and other operand types are INVALID_OPERAND, normally trapped as a non-match; intrinsic errors may instead be diagnosed statically as INVALID_GRAFT. Malformed EXPR syntax and RESOURCE_LIMIT remain fatal.

tests.name: Invalid computed EXPR name is a runtime mismatch
Wrapped CHARS is not exactly CHARS
Invalid operand after a known member
Missing imported class after a known member
